title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the 37th Batch of Guiding Cases
ruling_gist_en:
1. In cases involving the illegal discharge of oily wastewater from vessels, a people's court may determine the act of discharging pollutants and the resulting damage based on the vessel's navigation trajectory, the operational status of pollution prevention and control facilities, the disposal destination of pollutants, and evidence including the defendant's confession, witness testimony, and expert opinions.

2. Where, due to objective reasons, it is impossible to sample the oily wastewater illegally discharged from a vessel to determine whether it constitutes a toxic substance, an identification of the pollutant properties may be conducted based on residual bilge water from the same source and of stable nature.
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the 37th Batch of Guiding Cases

Fa [2022] No. 277

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Upon deliberation and decision by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, the ten cases (Guiding Cases No. 202-211), including the case of Wuhan Zhuohang Jianghai Trade Co., Ltd., Xiang Yang et al. (12 persons) — criminal附带 civil public interest litigation for environmental pollution, are hereby issued as the 37th batch of guiding cases for reference in the adjudication of similar cases.

December 30, 2022

Guiding Case No. 202

Wuhan Zhuohang Jianghai Trade Co., Ltd., Xiang Yang et al. (12 persons) — criminal附带 civil public interest litigation for environmental pollution

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and issued on December 30, 2022)

Keywords: criminal; criminal附带 civil public interest litigation; illegal discharge of oily bilge water from vessels; determination of damage; identification of pollutant nature

Ruling Gist

1. In cases of illegal discharge of oily bilge water from vessels, the people's court may determine the act of illegally discharging pollutants and the damage caused thereby based on the vessel's navigation trajectory, the operation status of pollution prevention facilities, the destination of pollutant disposal, combined with evidence such as the defendants' confessions, witness testimony, and expert opinions.

2. When determining whether the illegally discharged oily bilge water from a vessel is a toxic substance, if sampling is impossible due to objective reasons, the identification of the nature of the pollutant may be based on residual bilge water of the same source and stable nature.

Legal Provisions

Article 338 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended by the Criminal Law Amendment (VIII) effective as of May 1, 2011)

Article 59 of the Water Pollution Prevention and Control Law of the People's Republic of China (amended on June 27, 2017)

Basic Facts

The defendant entity, Wuhan Zhuohang Jianghai Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhuohang Company), engaged in domestic waterborne fixed-route cargo transportation business through leased vessels. The route of its operated vessel, Guoyu No. 1, was from Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province, via Wuhu City, Anhui Province, to Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province, and from Beilun Port, Ningbo City, returning to Nanjing City.

In accordance with laws and regulations, the defendant entity Zhuohang Company formulated the "Management Instructions for Preventing Pollution from Ships," which stipulated that the oily bilge water of the Guoyu No. 1 vessel could be discharged after treatment by an oil-water separator meeting standards, or could be received by a qualified third party. For years, the machinery department of the defendant entity Zhuohang Company did not purchase or replace the filter elements of the oil-water separator, rendering the vessel's oil-water separator unable to function normally. The deputy general manager in charge of the machinery department and others instructed staff to use purified water to replace the water sample from the outlet of the oil-water separator for inspection, conniving the vessel to evade supervision and carry out illegal discharge. The company also did not hand over the oily bilge water to a qualified third party for treatment, and the oily bilge water had no lawful disposal destination for a long time.

During the period from August 2017 to March 2019, the defendant Xiang Yang, who successively served as captain of the Guoyu No. 1 vessel, the defendants Yin Jianglin and Hu Guozheng, who served as chief engineers, together with other co-defendants, violated the law and illegally discharged oily bilge water from the vessel on five occasions. Subsequently, they purchased sewage reception certificates, filled them out themselves, and attached them to the oil record book to cope with inspections. In March 2019, upon a tip-off, the act of illegally discharging oily bilge water into the Yangtze River by the Guoyu No. 1 vessel and the tools used were seized.

After being brought to justice, the defendants including Xiang Yang confessed that the chief engineer of the Guoyu No. 1 vessel and others, for the company's benefit, repeatedly instructed the duty engineers and motormen of the engine department to evade supervision and refuse to implement the anti-pollution measures required by laws and regulations, and on five occasions from August 2017 to March 2019, illegally discharged bilge oily bilge water into the Yangtze River and offshore natural waters without treatment by the oil-water separator. The confessions of the defendants corroborated each other and were supported by witness testimony, and were consistent with the circumstances that the vessel involved operated on a fixed route year-round and the accumulation rate of oily bilge water and the frequency of illegal discharge were relatively stable, sufficient to establish the relevant facts of the case.

Because the oily bilge water discharged into the environment could no longer be sampled due to objective reasons, and given that the vessel involved had been operating on a fixed route year-round with a stable frequency of illegal discharge and no changes in equipment or operating procedures, the residual oily bilge water in the bilge and the oily bilge water discharged into the environment were of the same source and stable nature without any essential change. Therefore, samples were taken from the residual bilge water for testing. After identification, the bilge oily bilge water of the Guoyu No. 1 vessel was determined to be a "toxic substance." Expert assessment opinions on ecological environmental damage confirmed that using the virtual treatment cost method, the amount of ecological environmental damage caused by the five illegal discharges of oily bilge water was RMB 10,000 to RMB 37,500.

The Gulou District People's Procuratorate of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, simultaneously filed a criminal附带 civil public interest lawsuit, accusing the defendant entity Zhuohang Company and each defendant of the crime of environmental pollution, and requested that the defendant Zhuohang Company be ordered to pay the environmental damage compensation costs of RMB 23,750, expert assessment fees of RMB 9,000, and announcement fees of RMB 700 in this case.

Judgment

The Xuanwu District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, on July 16, 2020, rendered a criminal附带 civil judgment (Case No. (2020) Su 0102 Xing Chu 24), finding the defendant entity Zhuohang Company guilty of the crime of environmental pollution and sentencing it to a fine of RMB 40,000; for the crime of environmental pollution, the defendants Xiang Yang and the other eleven defendants were sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment ranging from one year and six months to eight months, and fines ranging from RMB 30,000 to RMB 10,000; the defendant in the civil public interest lawsuit, Zhuohang Company, was ordered to pay environmental damage compensation of RMB 23,750, expert assessment fees of RMB 9,000, and announcement fees of RMB 700, totaling RMB 33,450. After the judgment was announced, the defendant Xiang Yang appealed. The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, on December 23, 2020, rendered a criminal附带 civil ruling (Case No. (2020) Su 01 Xing Zhong 575), dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that: In accordance with laws and regulations such as the Water Pollution Prevention and Control Law, although the defendant entity Zhuohang Company had formulated pollution prevention measures for bilge oily bilge water, these measures were mere formality in actual operation and not implemented. The oil-water separator used for pollution prevention could not function normally. The defendant entity Zhuohang Company falsified test reports to obtain a pass for the oil-water separator water sample and purchased sewage reception certificates at low prices to evade supervision. The vessel involved operated on a fixed route year-round over thousands of kilometers, and with the increase in voyage, oily bilge water would inevitably be generated and accumulate continuously. However, the oily bilge water was neither treated by the oil-water separator nor handed over to a qualified third party for reception. The confessions of each defendant, witness testimony, and physical evidence in the case concerning the method, time, and participants of the illegal discharge were consistent with each other, sufficient to establish that each defendant committed the environmental pollution act of discharging oily bilge water into the Yangtze River and offshore waters. The nature of the involved oily bilge water was stable, the vessel operated on a fixed route year-round, the equipment, operating procedures, and generation mechanism of oily bilge water were stable, and the residual bilge oily bilge water was the same whole and consistent in characteristics as the illegally discharged bilge water, so samples could be taken for identification of the nature of the pollutant. After identification, the oily bilge water was determined to be a toxic substance.

The environmental pollution act in question was for the benefit of the defendant entity Zhuohang Company, under the instruction of the deputy general manager in charge, and involved the captain of the Guoyu No. 1 vessel, the chief engineer, motormen, and others jointly illegally discharging untreated bilge oily bilge water into the Yangtze River and offshore waters traversed. It should be determined as a unit crime. Zhuohang Company, in violation of national regulations, discharged toxic substances by evading supervision, seriously polluting the environment, and its act constituted the crime of environmental pollution. The defendants including Xiang Yang were the persons directly in charge or other persons directly responsible in the unit crime, and should be convicted and punished for the crime of environmental pollution.

The defendant in the civil public interest lawsuit, Zhuohang Company, polluted the environment and should bear liability for ecological environmental damage compensation according to law. Zhuohang Company illegally discharged untreated bilge oily bilge water into natural waters multiple times. The expert opinion quantified the amount of ecological environmental damage using the virtual treatment cost method, which was not inappropriate, and Zhuohang Company did not object to it. According to the assessment, the ecological environmental damage caused by the vessel's five illegal discharges of untreated bilge oily bilge water into the Yangtze River and offshore waters traversed amounted to RMB 10,000 to RMB 37,500. The public interest litigation plaintiff, the Gulou District People's Procuratorate of Nanjing, claimed the middle value of that range for the ecological environmental damage compensation, which had legal and factual basis and was supported according to law. The expert assessment fees and announcement fees claimed by the public interest litigation plaintiff were reasonable expenses incurred for the litigation and were supported according to law.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Jiang Li, Liu Shanglei, Yu Yuanzhu)

Guiding Case No. 203

Zuo Yong, Xu He — criminal附带 civil public interest litigation for environmental pollution

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and issued on December 30, 2022)

Keywords: criminal; criminal附带 civil public interest litigation; emergency response measures; necessary and reasonable scope; public and private property losses; ecological environmental damage

Ruling Gist

For necessary, reasonable, and appropriate environmental pollution disposal costs, the people's court shall determine that they fall within the scope of public and private property losses and ecological environmental damage compensation in criminal附带 civil public interest litigation cases for environmental pollution. For disposal costs that clearly exceed the necessary and reasonable scope, they shall not be used as a basis for pursuing the criminal liability of the defendants or for the defendant in the civil public interest litigation to bear liability for ecological environmental damage compensation.

Legal Provisions

Article 338 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended by the Criminal Law Amendment (VIII) effective as of May 1, 2011)

Basic Facts

Starting from June 2018, the defendant Zuo Yong rented a factory building in Cheqiao Town, Huai'an District, Huai'an City, Jiangsu Province, and produced aluminum ingots without approval. Later, the defendant Xu He and others, knowing that Zuo Yong did not have a hazardous waste operation license, still screened aluminum ash and produced aluminum ingots in the above factory building of Zuo Yong, generating a total of about 100 tons of waste aluminum ash. On April 23, 2019, Zuo Yong and Xu He arranged for personnel to excavate a pit in Daxing Village, Cheqiao Town, Huai'an District, Huai'an City, and dumped the above waste aluminum ash. When more than 20 tons were dumped, the waste aluminum ash heated up and emitted smoke, which was discovered and stopped by the public, who then reported it.

On April 24 of the same year, the former Environmental Protection Bureau of Huai'an District, Huai'an City, commissioned the Forensic Identification Institute of Jiangsu Xinrui Environmental Monitoring Co., Ltd. to sample and identify the waste aluminum ash in the pit, and commissioned Huai'an Xiangyu Environmental Testing Technology Co., Ltd. to sample and test the air and waste gas downwind of the pit. On April 28, the test by Huai'an Xiangyu Environmental Testing Technology Co., Ltd. showed that ammonia exceeded the standard downwind of the pit. On April 29, the identification by the Forensic Identification Institute of Jiangsu Xinrui Environmental Monitoring Co., Ltd. showed that among the 13 samples of the dumped waste aluminum ash, 4 samples had fluoride (leaching toxicity) exceeding the standard value, and the number of exceeded samples exceeded the corresponding lower limit specified in the "Technical Specification on Identification of Hazardous Waste" (HJ/T298-2007). The waste aluminum ash was determined to be a hazardous waste with leaching toxicity characteristics. The "National Hazardous Waste List" (2021 edition) stipulates that aluminum ash slag generated from the surface of molten aluminum during remelting, refining, alloying, and casting of waste aluminum and aluminum ingots, as well as salt slag and secondary aluminum ash generated during the recovery process of aluminum, are hazardous wastes.

On April 27 of the same year, the Cheqiao Town People's Government of Huai'an District, Huai'an City, organized personnel to stir and extinguish the burning waste aluminum ash with soil. The mixture of stirred waste aluminum ash and soil weighed 453.84 tons.

In November 2019, the Jiangsu Provincial Academy of Environmental Sciences, commissioned by the Cheqiao Town People's Government of Huai'an District, Huai'an City, prepared an emergency response plan stating that: The mixture of waste aluminum ash and soil involved had not undergone hazardous waste attribute identification due to funding and time issues. According to Article 10 of the Exemption Management List of the "National Hazardous Waste List" (2016 edition), it was recommended to dispose of it by co-processing in cement kilns. The academy's assessment of the ecological environmental damage of this incident concluded that: There was no personal injury in this pollution incident, but there was property damage. The costs mainly included property damage costs, emergency response costs, and ecological environmental damage costs. Property damage costs were the losses of farmers' wheat, rape, broad beans, and vegetables during the cleanup process, totaling RMB 3,400. Emergency response costs included emergency monitoring costs of RMB 7,800 (actually received RMB 7,200), cleanup costs for the mixture of waste aluminum ash and soil of RMB 76,161, and disposal costs temporarily estimated at RMB 1,000 per ton because disposal had not yet been carried out. Ecological environmental damage costs were RMB 18,000 (for pit backfilling and restoration, i.e., filling with soil).

On March 18, 2020, the Cheqiao Town People's Government of Huai'an District, Huai'an City, commissioned Nanjing Zhonglian Cement Co., Ltd. to dispose of the mixture of waste aluminum ash and soil as hazardous waste at a unit price of RMB 2,800 per ton, inclusive of tax and transportation costs. Additionally, identification fees of RMB 80,000 for Jiangsu Xinrui Environmental Monitoring Co., Ltd., emergency response plan fees of RMB 70,000 for the Jiangsu Provincial Academy of Environmental Sciences, and ecological environmental damage assessment fees of RMB 250,000 were incurred, totaling RMB 400,000.

Regarding the issues related to the emergency response in this case, the expert witness from the Jiangsu Provincial Academy of Environmental Sciences clarified in court that the emergency response plan targeted the already excavated mixture of waste aluminum ash and soil. This mixture could not be directly determined as hazardous waste; handling it under the exemption procedure could improve economy and practicality. The price for co-processing the contaminated soil in cement kilns in this case was RMB 1,000 per ton. A person with specialized knowledge appearing in court opined that aluminum ash does not burn over a large area; it is sufficient to cover the open flames with soil. After mixing 20 tons of waste aluminum ash with soil, the cleaned mixture should be within the range of 60 to 120 tons; otherwise, it constitutes excessive disposal.

The Huai'an District People's Procuratorate of Huai'an City filed a criminal附带 civil environmental public interest lawsuit, accusing the defendants Zuo Yong and Xu He of the crime of environmental pollution, and requested that the defendants Zuo Yong and Xu He jointly compensate for property damage costs of RMB 3,400, emergency response costs of RMB 1,431,788, ecological environmental damage costs of RMB 18,000, and other reasonable costs such as inspection and appraisal fees of RMB 400,000, totaling RMB 1,853,188; and that the defendants Zuo Yong and Xu He publicly apologize to the public in Huai'an city-level media.

Judgment

The Xuyi County People's Court of Jiangsu Province, on June 24, 2021, rendered a criminal附带 civil judgment (Case No. (2019) Su 0830 Xing Chu 534), finding the defendant Zuo Yong guilty of the crime of environmental pollution and sentencing him to two years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000; the defendant Xu He guilty of the crime of environmental pollution and sentencing him to two years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000; ordering the defendant Zuo Yong to return illegal gains of RMB 13,000 to the State Treasury; the defendants Zuo Yong and Xu He to jointly and severally compensate for property damage costs of RMB 3,400, emergency response costs of RMB 156,489, ecological environmental damage costs of RMB 18,000, and transactional costs such as appraisal and assessment fees of RMB 400,000, totaling RMB 577,889, to be paid within 15 days after the judgment becomes effective; ordering the defendants Zuo Yong and Xu He to publicly apologize to the public in Huai'an city-level media; and dismissing the other claims of the criminal附带 civil public interest litigation plaintiff, the Huai'an District People's Procuratorate of Huai'an City. After the judgment was announced, there was no appeal or protest, and the judgment became effective.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that: The defendants Zuo Yong and Xu He, in violation of national regulations, jointly dumped hazardous waste, seriously polluting the environment, and their acts constituted the crime of environmental pollution. The acts of the two defendants caused ecological environmental damage and harmed the public interest. In addition to criminal punishment, they should also bear corresponding civil liability according to law, including compensation for losses and apology. The defendants Zuo Yong and Xu He should jointly and severally bear liability for the consequences of the ecological environmental damage caused.

To safeguard national interests and social public interests, the claim of the criminal附带 civil public interest litigation plaintiff that the two defendants should bear liability for ecological environmental damage compensation shall be supported. However, the determination of the amount of ecological environmental damage should follow the principles of reasonableness and necessity. When a procuratorial authority initiates a public interest lawsuit, it should, based on the purpose of social public interest, the position of fairness and justice, and the principles of resource conservation and ecological environmental protection, reasonably put forward claims and accurately examine evidence. That is, after an environmental pollution accident occurs, the administrative authority's adoption of emergency response measures should be guided by the principles of necessity, reasonableness, and appropriateness. Necessary, reasonable, and appropriate disposal costs shall be used as the basis for pursuing the criminal liability of the defendants and for the defendants to bear liability for ecological environmental damage compensation. However, disposal costs that clearly exceed the necessary and reasonable scope shall not be identified as public and private property losses caused by the environmental pollution accident, and cannot be used as the basis for pursuing the criminal liability of the defendants, nor as the basis for the defendants to bear liability for ecological environmental damage compensation. The focus of this case is whether the emergency response measures exceeded the necessary and reasonable limits.

1. On the issue of whether the emergency response measure of covering more than 20 tons of waste aluminum ash with more than 400 tons of soil was reasonable and necessary

After an environmental pollution accident occurs, the means and methods of emergency response taken by the administrative authority to eliminate dangers, remove pollution, and prevent further expansion of damage should be recognized, but under the premise that conditions permit, the basic principle should still be necessary, reasonable, and appropriate disposal. In this case, after receiving the report and going to the scene for investigation, the relevant administrative authority had determined that the dumped substance was waste aluminum ash. Waste aluminum ash does not burn over a large area; even if local combustion occurs, it is sufficient to cover the open flames with soil. The disposal technique for waste aluminum ash, namely the "soil covering" technique, is relatively simple and universal. In this case, the emergency response took place several days after the pollution incident occurred, so there was no urgency in terms of time. The emergency response personnel had sufficient time to study and formulate more reasonable plans. The measure taken by the administrative authority to organize personnel to mix and stir with soil was feasible and could achieve the emergency effect, but the amount of soil used should be within a reasonable and necessary range; otherwise, it would not only cause excessive contaminated soil and consume national resources, but also increase corresponding disposal costs. The actual amount of mixture excavated in this case was nearly four times the maximum value recommended by experts, which was too large a discrepancy. The cleanup of 453.84 tons of mixture after stirring with soil in this environmental pollution incident constituted excessive disposal. In accordance with the principles of appropriate disposal and resource conservation, combined with expert opinions, the reasonable and necessary amount of mixture to be cleaned up in this pollution incident was determined to be 120 tons.

2. On the issue of whether it was reasonable to directly commission disposal of the mixture of waste aluminum ash and soil as hazardous waste at a price of RMB 2,800 per ton

The emergency response plan prepared by the Jiangsu Provincial Academy of Environmental Sciences clearly states that the transfer and disposal of the waste aluminum ash mixture involved in this case could be managed not as hazardous waste in accordance with Article 10 of the Exemption Management List of the National Hazardous Waste List (2016 Edition), and it suggested disposal by co-processing in cement kilns, with an estimated disposal cost of RMB 1,000/ton (including transportation costs). Therefore, the disposal and utilization of this mixture could be managed not as hazardous waste, and it was more reasonable to directly deliver it for disposal as contaminated soil at the price of RMB 1,000/ton. However, the disposal price in this case was too high, and the portion exceeding RMB 1,000/ton was not recognized.

III. Whether the loading and disbursement costs and transportation costs actually incurred but not included in the ecological environment damage assessment report should be included in the emergency response costs.

Upon investigation, when the emergency response personnel actually disposed of the mixture of waste aluminum ash and soil, they incurred loading and disbursement costs and transportation costs for the mixture. The appraiser who appeared in court clearly stated that the disposal cost of RMB 1,000/ton in the ecological environment damage assessment report included transportation costs but not loading and disbursement costs. Therefore, the additional transportation costs paid in the actual disposal were unreasonable and unnecessary, and thus were not supported. However, the loading and disbursement costs fell within the scope of "costs incurred by the plaintiff for taking reasonable preventive and disposal measures to cease the infringement, remove the obstruction, and eliminate the danger" as stipulated in Article 19 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases, and were therefore supported.

IV. Regarding the determination of the amount of public and private property losses and the amount of compensation in the incidental civil public interest litigation.

Upon investigation, the public and private property losses in this case included the direct property losses and the reduced actual value caused by the environmental pollution act, as well as the costs incurred for necessary and reasonable measures such as backfilling the contaminated site to prevent the spread of pollution and eliminate pollution, and the emergency monitoring costs for handling the sudden environmental incident. Based on the assessment by the Jiangsu Provincial Academy of Environmental Sciences and the actual disposal situation, the amounts of public and private property losses caused by the environmental pollution acts of defendants Zuo Yong and Xu He were determined as follows: 1. Property damage costs: RMB 3,400, i.e., the losses of wheat, rapeseed, broad beans, and vegetables of farmers during the cleanup process, totaling RMB 3,400. 2. Emergency response costs: RMB 156,489. Emergency response costs included: (1) emergency monitoring costs of RMB 7,200; (2) cleanup costs of RMB 20,137; (3) disposal costs of RMB 129,152. 3. Ecological environment damage costs: RMB 18,000. After the emergency cleanup of the pond, the pollution was basically eliminated, but backfilling and restoration were needed, with backfilling costs of RMB 18,000. The total of the above costs was RMB 177,889. That is, the amount of public and private property losses should be determined as RMB 177,889, which did not reach the RMB 1,000,000 stipulated in the judicial interpretation and did not constitute a particularly serious consequence.

The ecological environment damage amount claimed by the incidental civil public interest litigation plaintiff included the above-mentioned amount of public and private property losses, as well as the appraisal and assessment fees for ecological environment damage and the costs for preparing the emergency plan, totaling RMB 400,000. In summary, the total amount of ecological environment damages that defendants Zuo Yong and Xu He should bear was RMB 577,889.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Sun Zaitong, Jiang Yingying, Wang Yulin, Zhang Chunyan, Zhai Shunchang, Chen Zhiyi, Xue Qin)

Guiding Case No. 204

The Fifth Branch of the Chongqing Municipal People's Procuratorate v. Chongqing Yuhuang Electric Power Equipment Manufacturing Co., Ltd. et al. — environmental pollution civil public interest litigation

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and released on December 30, 2022)

Keywords: civil / environmental pollution civil public interest litigation / environmental protection technological transformation / expense offset / ecological environment damage compensation

Ruling Gist

1. Where the damaged ecological environment cannot be restored or restoration is unnecessary, and the tortfeasor, having already fulfilled the mandatory obligations stipulated by the ecological environment protection laws and regulations, carries out environmental protection technological transformation through means such as resource conservation, intensive recycling, if it is assessed that such transformation can achieve the effects of energy saving and emission reduction, pollution and carbon reduction, and risk reduction, the people's court may, upon the application of the tortfeasor, considering factors such as the time point of the environmental protection technological transformation and the compliance status with ecological environment protection laws, appropriately offset the costs of such environmental protection technological transformation against the ecological environment damage compensation that the tortfeasor should bear.

2. Where the costs of environmental protection technological transformation are incurred to meet the requirements of the environmental impact assessment, the pollutant discharge standards set in the pollutant discharge permit, or to fulfill other mandatory obligations stipulated by ecological environment protection laws and regulations, and the tortfeasor applies to offset such costs against the ecological environment damage compensation that it should bear, the people's court shall not support such application.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 36, Paragraph 1 of Article 40 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China
Article 3 of the Circular Economy Promotion Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

Chongqing Pengzhan Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Pengzhan Company), Chongqing Yuhuang Electric Power Equipment Manufacturing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuhuang Company), and Chongqing Shuntai Iron Tower Manufacturing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shuntai Company) all lacked qualification for hazardous waste operation. On April 10, 2015, Pengzhan Company entered into contracts with Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company respectively, stipulating that Pengzhan Company would sell hydrochloric acid to Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company at a price of RMB 420/ton, with Pengzhan Company bearing the transportation costs. The aforementioned price included the price of the hydrochloric acid sold and the costs for Pengzhan Company to transport the waste hydrochloric acid back for disposal. Starting from July 2015, after transporting the waste hydrochloric acid back from Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company, Pengzhan Company directly and illegally discharged the waste hydrochloric acid. From July 2015 to March 2016, Pengzhan Company illegally discharged at least 717.14 tons of waste hydrochloric acid in total, causing pollution to the Tiaodeng River. Upon assessment, the ecological environment damage amount for this incident was RMB 6,454,260, along with transactional costs of RMB 25,100 and appraisal fees of RMB 5,000. After the pollution incident occurred, Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company invested funds to carry out technological transformations in multiple aspects, such as acid mist collection and auxiliary plating tank regeneration systems, thereby improving their environmental protection level. The public interest litigation plaintiff, the Fifth Branch of the Chongqing Municipal People's Procuratorate, believed that Pengzhan Company, Yuhuang Company, and Shuntai Company should bear the losses caused by this environmental pollution incident, and thus filed a lawsuit with the people's court, requesting a judgment ordering Pengzhan Company, Yuhuang Company, and Shuntai Company to bear ecological environment damage compensation and appraisal fees totaling RMB 6,484,360, and to make a public apology to the public.

Judgment

The Fifth Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing rendered a civil judgment (2019) Yu 05 Min Chu No. 256 on November 29, 2019: 1. Defendant Pengzhan Company shall compensate for the ecological restoration costs of RMB 6,479,360 and technical consultation fees of RMB 5,000 arising from the illegal discharge of waste hydrochloric acid, totaling RMB 6,484,360, to be paid within ten days from the effective date of this judgment into the dedicated judicial ecological restoration fee account designated by this court. 2. Defendants Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company shall bear joint and several liability for the compensation amount of Defendant Pengzhan Company determined in Item 1 of this judgment, each in the amount of RMB 3,242,180. 3. Defendants Pengzhan Company, Yuhuang Company, and Shuntai Company shall make a public apology to the public in media at or above the municipal level in Chongqing within thirty days from the effective date of this judgment. After the judgment was pronounced, Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company appealed, and during the second instance, they filed an application for installment payment and a request for offset of their technological transformation costs. The Chongqing High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2020) Yu Min Zhong No. 387 on December 25, 2020: 1. Affirm Items 1 and 3 of the civil judgment (2019) Yu 05 Min Chu No. 256 of the Fifth Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing. 2. Revoke Item 2 of the civil judgment (2019) Yu 05 Min Chu No. 256 of the Fifth Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing. 3. Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company shall each bear joint and several liability for the ecological environment damage compensation payable by Pengzhan Company in the amount of RMB 3,242,180, and after providing effective guarantees to the Fifth Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing, shall pay in three installments in the proportions of 25%, 25%, and 50%. The specific payment times are: within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, each shall pay RMB 809,920 and technical consultation fees of RMB 2,500; by December 31, 2021, each shall pay RMB 809,920; by December 31, 2022, each shall pay RMB 1,619,840. The technical consultation fees shall be paid within ten days after the execution into the account designated by the Fifth Branch of the Chongqing Municipal People's Procuratorate. 4. If Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company carry out technological transformation after the effective date of this judgment, significantly reduce the generation of hazardous waste or reduce resource consumption under the same production capacity, and have not been punished for environmental violations, the technological transformation costs already paid by them may be offset against the third installment payment upon application to the people's court, supported by an assessment opinion on the effect of the technological transformation and an audit report on the capital invested in the technological transformation issued by a legally qualified intermediary institution.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that, according to Article 57 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Solid Waste Pollution (amended in 2015), units engaged in the collection, storage, and disposal of hazardous waste must apply for and obtain a business license from the administrative department of environmental protection of the people's government at or above the county level; units engaged in the utilization of hazardous waste must apply for and obtain a business license from the administrative department of environmental protection of the State Council or the administrative department of environmental protection of the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government. In this case, Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company, as producers of hazardous waste, handed over the hazardous waste involved to Pengzhan Company, which did not possess a hazardous waste business license, for disposal, thus violating the legal obligation to prevent and control hazardous waste pollution. Since it was impossible to distinguish the specific quantities or shares of hazardous waste provided by Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company respectively in the illegal discharge by Pengzhan Company, this constituted a joint tort, and therefore Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company should bear joint and several liability for the ecological environment damage caused by Pengzhan Company.

As an important litigation system established by the Environmental Protection Law, the purpose of environmental public interest litigation is not only to pursue environmental tort liability but, more importantly, to urge and guide environmental tortfeasors to carry out environmental restoration and encourage enterprises to follow the path of ecological priority and green development, achieving coordination between environmental protection and economic and social development. After the pollution incident involved in the case, Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company carried out technological transformation and requested that the technological transformation costs be offset against the ecological environment damage compensation. Regarding the issue of whether technological transformation costs can be used to offset the ecological environment damage compensation that should be borne, the court should adhere to the aforementioned concept of environmental justice, distinguish between the projects and purposes of the environmental protection technological transformation implemented by the enterprise, and treat them differently. If the projects and purposes of the environmental protection technological transformation implemented by the enterprise only meet its environmental impact assessment requirements, achieve the pollutant discharge standards set in the pollutant discharge permit, or fulfill other mandatory legal obligations, then the costs of such technological transformation should not be offset. If the enterprise, on the basis of having fully fulfilled the mandatory environmental protection obligations imposed by law, achieves effects such as higher resource utilization rates, reduced pollutant emissions, and improved comprehensive waste utilization rates through the use of clean energy, adoption of better technologies, processes, or equipment, then the costs of such technological transformation should be considered for offset.

In this case, due to the river's self-purification capacity, it is now unnecessary to carry out ecological restoration of the polluted water body. Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company are willing to continue with technological transformation, and the technological transformation they have committed to implement is conducive to the reduction, reuse, and recycling of pollutants, and also to reducing the local environmental risk. Therefore, offsetting the environmental protection technological transformation costs actually paid by Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company against the ecological environment damage compensation they should bear is in line with the purpose of environmental public interest litigation in safeguarding social public interests. To support the green transformation of enterprises and encourage Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company to invest more funds in energy conservation and emission reduction, the court set the maximum offset limit for each of Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company at 50% of the ecological environment damage compensation they should bear. Therefore, if Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company carry out technological transformation after the effective date of this judgment, significantly reduce the generation of hazardous waste or reduce resource consumption under the same production capacity, and have not been punished for environmental violations, the technological transformation costs already paid by them may be offset upon application to the people's court, supported by an assessment opinion on the effect of the technological transformation and an audit report on the capital invested in the technological transformation issued by a legally qualified intermediary institution.

In environmental civil public interest litigation cases, it is necessary to ensure that the damaged ecological environment is restored in a timely and effective manner, while also giving enterprises that correctly face their own environmental violations and are willing to actively assume environmental legal responsibility the opportunity to continue legal production and operation, achieving a balance between protecting the ecological environment and promoting economic development. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the production and operation of Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company were affected to a certain extent. After the incident, the two enterprises invested heavily in technological transformation, and some of the outstanding technological transformation costs had become due for payment. Both enterprises currently face certain operational difficulties. To promote development, stabilize expectations, and ensure people's livelihood, and to maximize the maintenance of the enterprises' continuous operation capabilities, the court adopted the opinion of Yuhuang Company and Shuntai Company requesting installment payment, granting them permission to pay the ecological environment damage compensation in three installments over two years.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Tang Yalin, Zhao Ling, Huang Cheng)

Guiding Case No. 205

The Third Branch of the Shanghai Municipal People's Procuratorate v. Langxi Huayuan Solid Waste Disposal Co., Ltd., Ningbo High-tech Zone Mitai Trade Co., Ltd., Huang Deting, Xue Qiang — environmental pollution civil public interest litigation

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and released on December 30, 2022)

Keywords: civil / environmental pollution civil public interest litigation / solid waste / smuggling / disposal costs

Ruling Gist

1. Where a tortfeasor smuggles solid waste, causing ecological environment damage or creating a significant risk of environmental pollution or ecological damage, and the authority designated by the state or the legal organization requests that the tortfeasor assume ecological environment tort liability in accordance with the law, the people's court shall support such request. Where a tortfeasor who has not been held criminally liable in a criminal case arising from the same act argues that it should not assume ecological environment tort liability, the people's court shall not support such argument.

2. Where solid waste that has illegally entered the country cannot be returned due to objective reasons, harmless disposal is a necessary measure to prevent the occurrence and spread of ecological environment damage, and the reasonable costs incurred shall be borne by the tortfeasor. Where the tortfeasor argues on the ground that the solid waste has been seized and confiscated by the administrative law enforcement authority and the disposal costs should be included in the administrative law enforcement costs, the people's court shall not support such defense.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 179, Article 187 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (applicable in this case are Article 4 and Article 15 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, which came into effect on July 1, 2010)

Basic Facts

The court found upon trial: In early 2015, the legal representative of Langxi Huayuan Solid Waste Disposal Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huayuan Company) contacted Huang Deting, intending to purchase imported solid waste containing copper. Huang Deting then contacted Chen Yajun, the actual operator of Ningbo High-tech Zone Mitai Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mitai Company), and Xue Qiang, and they agreed on a division of labor to carry out the importation of solid waste containing copper. In September of the same year, Xue Qiang organized a shipment of 138.66 tons of copper sludge in South Korea. Mitai Company prepared false customs declaration documents under the product name of copper ore sand and informed Huayuan Company of the import cargo list by fax or other means. Huayuan Company paid Mitai Company RMB 458,793.90 for the goods based on the quotation on the cargo list, and Huang Deting then declared the goods for import at the Shanghai port. The solid waste was subsequently seized by customs and detained in the port area, unable to be returned, threatening the ecological environment safety of our country. The Shanghai Solid Waste Management Center determined that the copper sludge involved contained a large amount of heavy metals and should be strictly managed, with harmless disposal entrusted to a unit with a hazardous waste business license. According to the assessment by the Shanghai Price Certification Center, the disposal costs for the copper sludge involved were RMB 1,053,700.

It was also found that on December 25, 2017, the Third Branch of the Shanghai Municipal People's Procuratorate filed a public prosecution with the Third Intermediate People's Court of Shanghai against Mitai Company, Huang Deting, and Xue Qiang for jointly smuggling solid waste prohibited from importation by the state. The Third Intermediate People's Court of Shanghai rendered a criminal judgment (2018) Hu 03 Xing Chu No. 8 on September 18, 2018, sentencing Mitai Company for the crime of smuggling waste to a fine of RMB 200,000; Huang Deting for the crime of smuggling waste to four years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 300,000; and Xue Qiang for the crime of smuggling waste to two years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000. This criminal judgment has become legally effective.

Judgment

The Third Intermediate People's Court of Shanghai rendered a civil judgment (2019) Hu 03 Min Chu No. 11 on September 5, 2019: Defendants Mitai Company, Huang Deting, Xue Qiang, and Huayuan Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, jointly and severally compensate for the disposal costs of the illegally imported solid waste (copper sludge) in the amount of RMB 1,053,700, to be paid into the special public interest litigation account of the Third Branch of the Shanghai Municipal People's Procuratorate. Huayuan Company appealed. The Shanghai High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2019) Hu Min Zhong No. 450 on December 25, 2020: Appeal dismissed, affirm the original judgment.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that the fact that an actor has not been held criminally liable in a crime of smuggling waste does not necessarily mean that the actor will not be held civilly liable in a civil public interest litigation. Whether civil liability should be borne needs to be determined in accordance with civil legal norms. If the elements of corresponding civil liability are met, the actor should still bear civil compensation liability. In this case, the relevant evidence could prove that Huayuan Company had common discussions with Mitai Company, Huang Deting, and Xue Qiang regarding the importation of copper sludge, and Huayuan Company was the demand side and initiator of the importation of copper sludge. It had a common intention to commit the tort, meeting the constitutive elements of jointly implementing an environmental civil tort.

For solid waste prohibited from importation by the state that has illegally entered the country, even if no actual ecological environment damage has been caused due to the seizure, there still exists a significant risk of infringement to the national ecological environment safety, and the tortfeasor should still bear the civil liability for eliminating the danger. The relevant actors should first bear the legal responsibility for returning the solid waste, and bear the costs of return themselves. In the event that the return is impossible, the ecological environment safety hazard and impact still objectively exist, and the actor should not be exempted from the legal liability for eliminating the pollution risk due to the inability to return. Therefore, in this case, the four defendants should jointly bear the civil liability for eliminating the danger.

针对非法入境而滞留境内的固体废物，无害化处置是消除危险的必要措施，相应的处置费用应由侵权行为人承担。为防止生态环境损害的发生，行为人应当承担为停止侵害、消除危险等采取合理预防、处置措施而发生的费用。案涉铜污泥无法退运，为消除环境污染危险，需要委托有关专业单位采取无害化处置，此系必要的、合理的预防处置措施。相关费用属于因消除污染危险而产生的费用，华远公司与其他各方应承担连带赔偿责任。侵权行为人以固体废物已被行政执法机关查扣没收，处置费用应纳入行政执法成本作为抗辩理由的，不应予以支持。

指导性案例206号

北京市人民检察院第四分院诉朱清良、朱清涛环境污染民事公益诉讼案

（最高人民法院审判委员会讨论通过2022年12月30日发布）

关键词 民事/环境污染民事公益诉讼/土壤污染/生态环境功能损失赔偿/生态环境修复/修复效果评估

裁判要点

1.两个以上侵权人分别实施污染环境、破坏生态行为造成同一损害，每一个侵权人的污染环境、破坏生态行为都不足以造成全部损害，部分侵权人根据修复方案确定的整体修复要求履行全部修复义务后，请求以代其他侵权人支出的修复费用折抵其应当承担的生态环境服务功能损失赔偿金的，人民法院应予支持。

2.对于侵权人实施的生态环境修复工程，应当进行修复效果评估。经评估，受损生态环境服务功能已经恢复的，可以认定侵权人已经履行生态环境修复责任。

相关法条

《中华人民共和国民法典》第1167条、第1229条（本案适用的是自2010年7月1日起实施的《中华人民共和国侵权责任法》第21条、第65条）

基本案情

2015年10月至12月，朱清良、朱清涛在承包土地内非法开采建筑用砂89 370.8立方米，价值人民币4 468 540元。经鉴定，朱清良二人非法开采的土地覆被类型为果园，地块内原生土壤丧失，原生态系统被完全破坏，生态系统服务能力严重受损，确认存在生态环境损害。鉴定机构确定生态环境损害恢复方案为将损害地块恢复为园林地，将地块内缺失土壤进行客土回填，下层回填普通土，表层覆盖60厘米种植土，使地块重新具备果树种植条件。恢复工程费用评估核算为2 254 578.58元。北京市人民检察院第四分院以朱清良、朱清涛非法开采造成土壤受损，破坏生态环境，损害社会公共利益为由提起环境民事公益诉讼（本案刑事部分另案审理）。

2020年6月24日，朱清良、朱清涛的代理人朱某某签署生态环境修复承诺书，承诺按照生态环境修复方案开展修复工作。修复工程自2020年6月25日开始，至2020年10月15日完成。2020年10月15日，北京市房山区有关单位对该修复工程施工质量进行现场勘验，均认为修复工程依法合规、施工安全有序开展、施工过程中未出现安全性问题、环境污染问题，施工程序、工程质量均符合修复方案要求。施工过程严格按照生态环境修复方案各项具体要求进行，回填土壤质量符合标准，地块修复平整，表层覆盖超过60厘米的种植土，已重新具备果树种植条件。

上述涉案土地内存在无法查明的他人倾倒的21 392.1立方米渣土，朱清良、朱清涛在履行修复过程中对该部分渣土进行环境清理支付工程费用75.4万元。

裁判结果

北京市第四中级人民法院于2020年12月21日作出（2020）京04民初277号民事判决：一、朱清良、朱清涛对其造成的北京市房山区长阳镇朱岗子村西的14 650.95平方米土地生态环境损害承担恢复原状的民事责任，确认朱清良、朱清涛已根据《房山区朱清良等人盗采砂石矿案生态环境损害鉴定评估报告书》确定的修复方案将上述受损生态环境修复到损害发生之前的状态和功能（已履行完毕）。二、朱清良、朱清涛赔偿生态环境受到损害至恢复原状期间的服务功能损失652 896.75元；朱清良、朱清涛在履行本判决第一项修复义务时处理涉案地块上建筑垃圾所支付费用754 000元折抵其应赔偿的生态环境受到损害至恢复原状期间的服务功能损失652 896.75元。三、朱清良、朱清涛于本判决生效之日起七日内给付北京市人民检察院第四分院鉴定费115 000元。四、朱清良、朱清涛在一家全国公开发行的媒体上向社会公开赔礼道歉，赔礼道歉的内容及媒体、版面、字体需经本院审核，朱清良、朱清涛应于本判决生效之日起十五日内向本院提交，并于审核通过之日起三十日内刊登，如未履行上述义务，则由本院选择媒体刊登判决主要内容，所需费用由朱清良、朱清涛负担。判决后，双方当事人均未提出上诉。

裁判理由

法院生效裁判认为：朱清良、朱清涛非法开采的行为，造成了生态环境破坏，侵害了不特定多数人的合法权益，损害了社会公共利益，构成环境民事侵权。朱清良、朱清涛作为非法开采行为人，违反了保护环境的法定义务，应对造成的生态环境损害承担民事责任。

一、关于被告对他人倾倒渣土的处理费用能否折抵生态功能损失赔偿费用的问题。从环境法的角度而言，生态环境具有供给服务、调节服务、文化服务、以及支持服务等功能。生态环境受损将导致其向公众或其他生态系统提供上述服务的功能减少或丧失。朱清良、朱清涛在其租赁的林果地上非法开采，造成地块土壤受损，属于破坏生态环境、损害社会公共利益的行为，还应赔偿生态环境受到损害至恢复原状期间的服务功能损失。根据鉴定评估报告对生态服务价值损失的评估意见，确定朱清良、朱清涛应承担的服务功能损失赔偿金额为652 896.75元。《最高人民法院关于审理环境民事公益诉讼案件适用法律若干问题的解释》第二十四条第一款规定，人民法院判决被告承担的生态环境修复费用、生态环境受到损害至恢复原状期间服务功能损失等款项，应当用于修复被损害的生态环境。故被告承担的生态环境受到损害至恢复原状期间服务功能损失的款项应当专项用于该案环境修复、治理或异地公共生态环境修复、治理。朱清良、朱清涛对案涉土地进行生态修复时，土地上还存在无法查明的他人倾倒渣土。朱清涛、朱清良非法开采的行为造成受损地块原生土壤丧失、土壤的物理结构变化，而他人倾倒渣土的行为则会造成土壤养分的改变，两个侵权行为叠加造成现在的土壤生态环境损害。为全面及时恢复生态环境，朱清良、朱清涛根据修复方案对涉案地块整体修复的要求，对该环境内所倾倒渣土进行清理并为此实际支出75.4万元，系属于对案涉环境积极的修复、治理，这与法律、司法解释规定的被告承担生态功能损失赔偿责任的目的和效果是一致的。同时，侵权人在承担修复责任的同时，积极采取措施，对他人破坏环境造成的后果予以修复治理，有益于生态环境保护，在修复效果和综合治理上亦更能体现及时优化生态环境的特点。因此，综合两项费用的功能目的以及赔偿费用专项执行的实际效果考虑，朱清良、朱清涛对倾倒渣土环境进行清理的费用可以折抵朱清良、朱清涛需要承担的生态功能损失赔偿费用。

二、关于被告诉讼过程中自行进行生态修复的效果评估问题。朱清良、朱清涛在诉讼过程中主动履行环境修复义务，并于2020年6月25日至10月15日期间按照承诺书载明的生态环境修复方案对案涉地块进行了回填修复。根据《最高人民法院关于审理生态环境损害赔偿案件的若干规定（试行）》第九条规定，负有相关环境资源保护监督管理职责的部门或者其委托的机构在行政执法过程中形成的事件调查报告、检验报告、监测报告、评估报告、监测数据等，经当事人质证并符合证据标准的，可以作为认定案件事实的根据。本案中，北京市房山区有关单位积极履行环境监督管理职责，对于被告自行实施的生态修复工程进行过程监督并出具相应的验收意见，符合其职责范围，且具备相应的专业判断能力，有关单位联合出具的验收意见，可以作为认定当事人自行实施的生态修复工程质量符合标准的重要依据。同时，评估机构在此基础上，对修复工程进行了效果评估，确认案涉受损地块内土壤已恢复至基线水平，据此可以认定侵权人已经履行生态环境修复责任。

江苏省南京市人民检察院诉王玉林生态破坏民事公益诉讼案

（最高人民法院审判委员会讨论通过2022年12月30日发布）

关键词 民事/生态破坏民事公益诉讼/非法采矿/生态环境损害/损失整体认定/系统保护修复

裁判要点

1.人民法院审理环境民事公益诉讼案件，应当坚持山水林田湖草沙一体化保护和系统治理。对非法采矿造成的生态环境损害，不仅要对造成山体（矿产资源）的损失进行认定，还要对开采区域的林草、水土、生物资源及其栖息地等生态环境要素的受损情况进行整体认定。

2.人民法院审理环境民事公益诉讼案件，应当充分重视提高生态环境修复的针对性、有效性，可以在判决侵权人承担生态环境修复费用时，结合生态环境基础修复及生物多样性修复方案，确定修复费用的具体使用方向。

相关法条

《中华人民共和国环境保护法》第64条

《中华人民共和国民法典》第1165条（本案适用的是自2010年7月1日起实施的《中华人民共和国侵权责任法》第6条）

基本案情

2015年至2018年期间，王玉林违反国家管理矿产资源法律规定，在未取得采矿许可证的情况下，使用机械在南京市浦口区永宁镇老山林场原山林二矿老宕口内、北沿山大道建设施工红线外非法开采泥灰岩、泥页岩等合计十余万吨。南京市浦口区人民检察院以王玉林等人的行为构成非法采矿罪向南京市玄武区人民法院提起公诉。该案审理期间，王玉林已退赔矿石资源款4 455 998.6元。2020年3月、8月，江苏省环境科学研究院先后出具《“南京市浦口区王玉林等人非法采矿案”生态环境损害评估报告》（以下简称《评估报告》）《“南京市浦口区王玉林等人非法采矿案”生态环境损害（动物类）补充说明》（以下简称《补充说明》）。南京市人民检察院认为，王玉林非法采矿造成国家矿产资源和生态环境破坏，损害社会公共利益，遂提起本案诉讼，诉请判令王玉林承担生态破坏侵权责任，赔偿生态环境损害修复费用1 893 112元（具体包括：1.生态资源的损失中林木的直接经济损失861 750元；2.生态系统功能受到影响的损失：森林涵养水损失440 233元；水土流失损失50 850元；土壤侵蚀损失81 360元；树木放氧量减少损失64 243元；鸟类生态价值损失243 122元；哺乳动物栖息地服务价值损失18 744元；3.修复期间生物多样性的价值损失132 810元）以及事务性费用400 000元，并提出了相应的修复方案。

裁判结果

江苏省南京市中级人民法院于2020年12月4日作出（2020）苏01民初798号民事判决：一、被告王玉林对其非法采矿造成的生态资源损失1 893 112元（已缴纳）承担赔偿责任，其中1 498 436元用于南京市山林二矿生态修复工程及南京市浦口区永宁街道大桥林场路口地质灾害治理工程，394 676元用于上述地区生物多样性的恢复及保护。二、被告王玉林承担损害评估等事务性费用400 000元（已缴纳），该款项于本判决生效后十日内划转至南京市人民检察院。判决后，南京市人民检察院与王玉林均未上诉，判决已发生法律效力。

裁判理由

法院生效裁判认为：非法采矿对生态资源造成复合性危害，在长江沿岸非法露天采矿，不仅造成国家矿产资源损失，还必然造成开采区域生态环境破坏及生态要素损失。环境和生物之间、生物和生物之间协同共生，相互影响、相互依存，形成动态的平衡。一个生态要素的破坏，必然会对整个生态系统的多个要素造成不利影响。非法采矿将直接导致开采区域的植被和土壤破坏，山体损坏影响到林、草蓄积，林、草减少影响到水土涵养，上述生态要素的破坏又直接、间接影响到鸟类和其他动物的栖息环境，造成生态系统的整体破坏及生物多样性的减少，自然要素生态利益的系统损害必将最终影响到人类的生产生活和优美生态环境的实现。被告王玉林违反矿产资源法的规定，未取得采矿许可证即实施非法采矿行为，造成生态环境的破坏，主观存在过错，非法采矿行为与生态环境损害之间具有因果关系，应当依照《中华人民共和国侵权责任法》第六条之规定，对其行为造成的生态环境损害后果承担赔偿责任。

一、关于生态环境损害计算问题

（一）生态资源的经济损失计算合理。非法采矿必将使被开采区域的植被遭到严重破坏，受损山体的修复及自然林地的恢复均需要合理周期，即较长时间才能重新恢复林地的生态服务功能水平，故《评估报告》以具有20年生长年限的林地作为参照计算具有一定合理性，《评估报告》制作人关于林木经济损失计算的解释科学，故应对非法采矿行为造成林木经济损失861 750元依法予以认定。

（二）鸟类生态价值损失计算恰当。森林资源为鸟类提供了栖息地和食物来源，鸟类种群维持着食物链的完整性，保持营养物质循环的顺利进行，栖息地的破坏必然导致林鸟迁徙或者食物链条断裂，一旦食物链的完整性被破坏，必将对整个森林生态系统产生严重的后果。《补充说明》载明，两处非法开采点是林鸟种群的主要栖息地和适宜生境，非法采矿行为造成鸟类栖息地被严重破坏，由此必然产生种子传播收益额及改善土壤收益额的损失。鸟类为种子的主要传播者和捕食者，可携带或者吞食植物种子，有利于生态系统次生林的自然演替；同时，次生林和原始森林系统的良性循环，也同样为鸟类的自然栖息地提供了庇护，对植物种子的传播具有积极意义。《补充说明》制作人从生态系统的完整性和种间生态平衡的角度，对非法采矿行为造成平衡性和生物多样性的破坏等方面对鸟类传播种子损失作出了详细解释，解释科学合理，故对非法采矿造成鸟类生态价值损失243 122元予以认定。

（三）哺乳动物栖息地服务价值损失客观存在。森林生态系统是陆地生态系统的重要组成部分，同时也是哺乳动物繁衍和生存的主要栖息地之一。哺乳动物不仅对维持生态系统平衡有重要作用，还能够调节植物竞争，维护系统物种多样性以及参与物质和能量循环等，是改变生态系统内部各构件配置的最基本动力。虽然因客观因素无法量化栖息地生态环境损害价值，但非法采矿行为造成山体破坏和植被毁坏，导致哺乳动物过境受到严重影响，哺乳动物栖息地服务价值损失客观存在。结合案涉非法采矿区域位于矿坑宕口及林场路口的实际情况，综合考虑上述区域植被覆盖率以及人类活动影响造成两区域内哺乳动物的种类和数量较少等客观因素，公益诉讼起诉人主张按照其他生态环境损失1 874 368元的1%计算哺乳动物栖息地服务价值损失18 744元具有一定的合理性，应当依法予以支持。For solid waste that has entered and remains within the territory through illegal entry, harmless disposal is a necessary measure to eliminate the danger, and the corresponding disposal costs shall be borne by the tortfeasor. To prevent the occurrence of ecological and environmental damage, the tortfeasor shall bear the costs incurred for taking reasonable preventive and disposal measures such as cessation of infringement and elimination of danger. The copper sludge involved in the case could not be returned for shipment. To eliminate the danger of environmental pollution, it was necessary to entrust relevant specialized units to carry out harmless disposal. This constituted a necessary and reasonable preventive disposal measure. The relevant expenses are costs arising from the elimination of pollution danger, and Huayuan Company and the other parties shall bear joint and several liability for compensation. Where a tortfeasor defends on the ground that the solid waste has been seized and confiscated by administrative law enforcement authorities and that disposal costs should be included in administrative enforcement costs, such defense shall not be supported.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Yin Yonglei, Zhang Xinquan, Chen Zhenyu)

Guiding Case No. 206

The Fourth Branch of Beijing Municipal People's Procuratorate v. Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao — civil public interest litigation for environmental pollution

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, promulgated on December 30, 2022)

Keywords: civil / civil public interest litigation for environmental pollution / soil contamination / compensation for loss of ecological environment functions / ecological environment restoration / restoration effectiveness assessment

Ruling Gist

1. Where two or more tortfeasors, through separate acts of polluting the environment or damaging the ecology, cause the same harm, and the act of each tortfeasor alone is insufficient to cause the entire harm, if some tortfeasors fulfill all restoration obligations in accordance with the overall restoration requirements set forth in the restoration plan, and request that the restoration costs they paid on behalf of other tortfeasors be offset against the compensation they are liable to pay for the loss of ecological environment service functions, the people's court shall support such request.

2. A restoration effectiveness assessment shall be conducted for the ecological environment restoration project implemented by the tortfeasor. If, upon assessment, the damaged ecological environment service functions have been restored, it may be determined that the tortfeasor has fulfilled its ecological environment restoration obligation.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Articles 1167 and 1229 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Articles 21 and 65 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, effective from July 1, 2010, are applicable in this case)

Basic Facts

From October to December 2015, Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao illegally mined 89,370.8 cubic meters of construction sand from contracted land, valued at RMB 4,468,540. Appraisal confirmed that the land cover type of the area illegally mined by the two Zhus was orchard; the native soil in the plot was lost, the original ecosystem was completely destroyed, and the ecosystem service capacity was severely impaired, confirming the existence of ecological environmental damage. The appraisal institution determined that the restoration plan for the ecological environmental damage was to restore the damaged plot to garden land, backfill the missing soil in the plot with foreign soil, backfill the lower layer with ordinary soil, and cover the surface layer with 60 centimeters of planting soil, so that the plot could once again meet the conditions for fruit tree cultivation. The restoration project cost was assessed at RMB 2,254,578.58. The Fourth Branch of Beijing Municipal People's Procuratorate filed an environmental civil public interest lawsuit (the criminal part of the case was tried separately) on the grounds that the illegal mining by Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao caused soil damage, destroyed the ecological environment, and harmed the public interest.

On June 24, 2020, Agent Zhu Moumou, on behalf of Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao, signed a commitment letter for ecological environment restoration, promising to carry out restoration work in accordance with the ecological environment restoration plan. The restoration project commenced on June 25, 2020 and was completed on October 15, 2020. On October 15, 2020, relevant units in Fangshan District, Beijing conducted an on-site inspection of the construction quality of the restoration project and all considered that the restoration project complied with laws and regulations, construction was carried out safely and orderly, no safety or environmental pollution issues occurred during construction, and the construction procedures and project quality met the requirements of the restoration plan. The construction process strictly followed all specific requirements of the ecological environment restoration plan. The quality of the backfilled soil met the standards, the plot was restored and leveled, the surface layer was covered with more than 60 centimeters of planting soil, and the plot has regained the conditions for fruit tree cultivation.

On the above-mentioned involved land, there was 21,392.1 cubic meters of construction waste dumped by unidentified third parties. During the implementation of the restoration, Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao paid engineering costs of RMB 754,000 for environmental cleanup of this portion of construction waste.

Judgment

The Beijing No. 4 Intermediate People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2020) Jing 04 Min Chu No. 277 on December 21, 2020: 1. Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao shall bear civil liability for restoring the original condition of the ecological environment damage to the 14,650.95 square meters of land located west of Zhugangzi Village, Changyang Town, Fangshan District, Beijing, caused by them. It is confirmed that Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao have restored the aforementioned damaged ecological environment to the state and function existing before the damage occurred in accordance with the restoration plan determined in the "Appraisal and Assessment Report on Ecological Environment Damage Caused by Zhu Qingliang and Others' Illegal Sand and Stone Mining Case in Fangshan District" (obligation fulfilled). 2. Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao shall compensate for the loss of service functions during the period from the occurrence of ecological environment damage to the restoration of the original state, in the amount of RMB 652,896.75. The expenses of RMB 754,000 paid by Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao for the disposal of construction waste on the involved plot during the performance of the restoration obligation under item 1 of this judgment shall be offset against the compensation they are liable to pay for the loss of service functions during the period from the occurrence of ecological environment damage to the restoration of the original state, amounting to RMB 652,896.75. 3. Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao shall pay the Fourth Branch of Beijing Municipal People's Procuratorate the appraisal fee of RMB 115,000 within seven days from the effective date of this judgment. 4. Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao shall make a public apology to society in a nationally distributed media outlet. The content of the apology and the media, layout, and font must be reviewed by this court. Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao shall submit the apology to this court within fifteen days from the effective date of this judgment and publish it within thirty days from the date of approval. If they fail to fulfill the above obligations, this court shall select a media outlet to publish the main contents of the judgment, and the expenses shall be borne by Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao. After the judgment, neither party appealed.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that the illegal mining acts of Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao caused ecological environment damage, infringed upon the legitimate rights and interests of an unspecified number of persons, harmed the public interest, and constituted environmental civil tort. As the perpetrators of the illegal mining, Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao violated their legal duty to protect the environment and shall bear civil liability for the ecological environment damage caused.

I. The issue of whether the costs incurred by the defendants for disposing of construction waste dumped by others can be offset against the compensation for loss of ecological functions.

From the perspective of environmental law, the ecological environment has functions such as provisioning services, regulating services, cultural services, and supporting services. Damage to the ecological environment will result in a reduction or loss of its ability to provide the above services to the public or other ecosystems. The illegal mining by Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao on their leased forest and fruit land caused soil damage to the plot, which is an act of destroying the ecological environment and harming the public interest. They should also compensate for the loss of service functions during the period from the occurrence of ecological environment damage to the restoration of the original state. Based on the appraisal opinion in the assessment report on the loss of ecological service value, the amount of compensation for loss of service functions to be borne by Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao was determined to be RMB 652,896.75. Article 24, paragraph 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation stipulates that sums such as ecological environment restoration costs and compensation for loss of service functions during the period from damage to restoration of original state, which the people's court orders the defendant to bear, shall be used for the restoration of the damaged ecological environment. Therefore, the sums borne by the defendants for loss of service functions during the period from damage to restoration of original state shall be used specifically for environmental restoration and remediation of that case or for public ecological environment restoration and remediation elsewhere. When Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao were carrying out ecological restoration on the involved land, there was still construction waste dumped by unidentified third parties on the land. The illegal mining acts of Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao caused the loss of native soil and changes in the physical structure of the soil in the damaged plot, while the act of others dumping construction waste would cause changes in soil nutrients. The two tortious acts combined resulted in the current soil ecological environment damage. To fully and timely restore the ecological environment, Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao, in accordance with the requirement of overall restoration of the involved plot in the restoration plan, cleaned up the construction waste dumped in that environment and actually incurred RMB 754,000 for this purpose. This constitutes active restoration and remediation of the involved environment, which is consistent with the purpose and effect of the defendant's liability for compensation for loss of ecological functions as provided by law and judicial interpretation. At the same time, while bearing the restoration liability, the tortfeasors actively took measures to restore and remediate the consequences of environmental damage caused by others, which is beneficial to ecological environmental protection and better reflects the characteristic of promptly optimizing the ecological environment in terms of restoration effect and comprehensive governance. Therefore, considering comprehensively the functional purposes of the two types of costs and the actual effect of the special implementation of compensation sums, the costs incurred by Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao for cleaning up the environment where construction waste was dumped can be offset against the compensation for loss of ecological functions that Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao need to bear.

II. The issue of assessing the effectiveness of ecological restoration carried out by the defendants themselves during the litigation process.

Zhu Qingliang and Zhu Qingtao actively fulfilled their environmental restoration obligations during the litigation process and, from June 25 to October 15, 2020, carried out backfill restoration on the involved plot in accordance with the ecological environment restoration plan stated in the commitment letter. According to Article 9 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Trial of Ecological Environmental Damage Compensation Cases (for Trial Implementation), incident investigation reports, inspection reports, monitoring reports, assessment reports, monitoring data, etc., formed during administrative law enforcement by departments with relevant environmental resource protection and supervision responsibilities or institutions entrusted by them, may, after being cross-examined by the parties and meeting evidentiary standards, be used as the basis for determining the facts of the case. In this case, the relevant units in Fangshan District, Beijing, actively performed their environmental supervision duties, supervised the process of the ecological restoration project implemented by the defendants themselves, and issued corresponding acceptance opinions, which was within their scope of duties and they possessed corresponding professional judgment capabilities. The acceptance opinions jointly issued by the relevant units can serve as an important basis for determining that the quality of the ecological restoration project implemented by the parties themselves meets the standards. At the same time, the appraisal institution, based on this, conducted an effectiveness assessment of the restoration project and confirmed that the soil in the damaged plot involved in the case had been restored to baseline levels. Based on this, it can be determined that the tortfeasors have fulfilled their ecological environment restoration responsibilities.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Ma Jun, Mei Yu, Zhao Jia, Wang Pengyu, Zhang Guirong, Zhang Fengguang, Heng Jun)

Guiding Case No. 207

Nanjing Municipal People's Procuratorate, Jiangsu Province v. Wang Yulin — civil public interest litigation for ecological damage

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, promulgated on December 30, 2022)

Keywords: civil / civil public interest litigation for ecological damage / illegal mining / ecological environment damage / overall determination of loss / systematic protection and restoration

Ruling Gist

1. When hearing environmental civil public interest litigation cases, the people's court shall adhere to the integrated protection and systematic governance of mountains, waters, forests, farmlands, lakes, grasslands, and deserts. For ecological environment damage caused by illegal mining, not only the loss of the mountain body (mineral resources) shall be determined, but also the damage to ecological environment elements such as forests, grasslands, water, soil, biological resources, and their habitats in the mining area shall be determined as a whole.

2. When hearing environmental civil public interest litigation cases, the people's court shall fully emphasize improving the targeted and effective nature of ecological environment restoration. When adjudging the tortfeasor to bear ecological environment restoration costs, the court may, in conjunction with the basic ecological restoration plan and the biodiversity restoration plan, determine the specific direction for the use of the restoration costs.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 64 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China

Article 1165 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Article 6 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, effective from July 1, 2010, is applicable in this case)

Basic Facts

During the period from 2015 to 2018, Wang Yulin, violating the provisions of national laws on the management of mineral resources and without obtaining a mining license, used machinery to illegally mine a total of over 100,000 tons of marl, mud shale, etc. from within the old pit of the former Shanlin No. 2 Mine in Laoshan Forest Farm, Yongning Town, Pukou District, Nanjing, and outside the construction red line of the Beiyanshan Avenue project. The Pukou District People's Procuratorate of Nanjing filed a public prosecution with the Xuanwu District People's Court of Nanjing, alleging that the acts of Wang Yulin and others constituted the crime of illegal mining. During the trial of that case, Wang Yulin had already returned the value of the ore resources, RMB 4,455,998.6. In March and August 2020, the Jiangsu Provincial Academy of Environmental Sciences successively issued the "Ecological Environment Damage Assessment Report for the 'Wang Yulin and Others Illegal Mining Case in Pukou District, Nanjing'" (hereinafter referred to as the "Assessment Report") and the "Supplementary Explanation on Ecological Environment Damage (Fauna) for the 'Wang Yulin and Others Illegal Mining Case in Pukou District, Nanjing'" (hereinafter referred to as the "Supplementary Explanation"). The Nanjing Municipal People's Procuratorate believed that Wang Yulin's illegal mining caused damage to national mineral resources and the ecological environment, harming the public interest, and therefore filed this lawsuit, requesting the court to order Wang Yulin to bear tort liability for ecological damage and to compensate for ecological environment damage restoration costs of RMB 1,893,112 (specifically including: 1. Within the loss of ecological resources, direct economic loss of forest trees: RMB 861,750; 2. Losses from affected ecosystem functions: loss of forest water conservation: RMB 440,233; loss of soil erosion: RMB 50,850; loss of soil erosion: RMB 81,360; loss from reduced tree oxygen release: RMB 64,243; loss of bird ecological value: RMB 243,122; loss of mammal habitat service value: RMB 18,744; 3. Loss of biodiversity value during the restoration period: RMB 132,810) as well as transactional costs of RMB 400,000, and proposed a corresponding restoration plan.

Judgment

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered the civil judgment (2020) Su 01 Min Chu No. 798 on December 4, 2020: 1. Defendant Wang Yulin shall bear liability for compensation for the ecological resource loss of RMB 1,893,112 (already paid) caused by his illegal mining, of which RMB 1,498,436 shall be used for the ecological restoration project of Shanlin No. 2 Mine in Nanjing and the geological disaster control project at the entrance of Daqiao Forest Farm, Yongning Street, Pukou District, Nanjing, and RMB 394,676 shall be used for the restoration and protection of biodiversity in the above areas. 2. Defendant Wang Yulin shall bear transactional costs such as damage assessment totaling RMB 400,000 (already paid), and this amount shall be transferred to the Nanjing Municipal People's Procuratorate within ten days from the effective date of this judgment. After the judgment, neither the Nanjing Municipal People's Procuratorate nor Wang Yulin appealed, and the judgment has become legally effective.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that illegal mining causes composite harm to ecological resources. Illegal open-pit mining along the Yangtze River not only results in the loss of national mineral resources but also inevitably leads to ecological environment damage and loss of ecological elements in the mining area. The environment and organisms, and organisms among themselves, coexist synergistically, interacting and depending on each other, forming a dynamic balance. The destruction of one ecological element will inevitably cause adverse effects on multiple elements of the entire ecosystem. Illegal mining will directly lead to the destruction of vegetation and soil in the mining area; damage to the mountain body affects forest and grass accumulation; the reduction of forests and grasses affects water and soil conservation; the destruction of the above ecological elements in turn directly and indirectly affects the habitat environment of birds and other animals, causing overall damage to the ecosystem and a reduction in biodiversity. The systematic damage to the ecological interests of natural elements will ultimately affect human production and life and the realization of a beautiful ecological environment. Defendant Wang Yulin, in violation of the provisions of the Mineral Resources Law, carried out illegal mining without obtaining a mining license, causing damage to the ecological environment. He was subjectively at fault, and there is a causal relationship between the illegal mining act and the ecological environment damage. Therefore, he shall bear compensatory liability for the ecological environment damage consequences caused by his acts in accordance with Article 6 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China.

I. The issue of calculating ecological environment damage

(1) The calculation of economic loss to ecological resources is reasonable. Illegal mining will inevitably cause severe damage to vegetation in the mining area. The restoration of the damaged mountain body and the recovery of natural forest land both require a reasonable period, meaning a longer time is needed to restore the level of ecological service functions of the forest land. Therefore, the Assessment Report's use of forest land with a growth period of 20 years as a reference for calculation has certain reasonableness. The explanation by the preparer of the Assessment Report regarding the calculation of economic loss of forest trees is scientific. Therefore, the economic loss of forest trees of RMB 861,750 caused by the illegal mining act should be determined in accordance with the law.

(2) The calculation of the loss of bird ecological value is appropriate. Forest resources provide habitats and food sources for birds. Bird populations maintain the integrity of the food chain and ensure the smooth progress of nutrient cycling. The destruction of habitats will inevitably lead to the migration of forest birds or the breaking of the food chain. Once the integrity of the food chain is destroyed, it will inevitably have serious consequences for the entire forest ecosystem. The Supplementary Explanation states that the two illegal mining sites were the main habitats and suitable habitats for forest bird populations. The illegal mining act caused severe damage to bird habitats, inevitably resulting in the loss of seed dispersal benefits and soil improvement benefits. Birds are the main dispersers and predators of seeds; they can carry or swallow plant seeds, which is beneficial for the natural succession of secondary forests in the ecosystem.
